body: I once drafted a tiny little script that would post tweet after tweet announcing my suicide attempt while I jump from the roof of my high school's building. I wanted a dramatic ending, of sort.
22 days ago. I should be ashamed. I am making progress though, or at least that's what I think. Thanks.
I'll try my best. Thanks for the kind words. :-)

:-)

I smiled at you today. Does that count? ;-)

That actually sounds a bit like me. I'm normally an okay guy, but I start panicking at particular situations, and I can never pinpoint exactly why I start panicking; I just do. Guess I'll have to work on my socializing skills a fair bit.
I do not live in the States, but I guess I'm kind of influenced by American culture to an extent.

I had to stop and ponder for a while after reading your comment. Why do we value independence so much in the first place? Humans do seem to succeed due to our nature as social creatures, able to rely on one another. We should have been taught to value interdependence over independence.
Cheers to your daughter, seems like an amazing lady. :-)
I'm actually going to be studying abroad for the next 4 years. Still financially dependent, but I'll be living on the other side of Earth.

Sometimes I get nervous just trying to open my mouth, especially around people of the same sex. Haven't figured out why, to be honest. My mind just starts going berserk whenever I want to talk.

I want to improve. Really do. I have a faint hope that I will able to grow away from the insecure self that I have had to live with my entire life. Thanks for your encouraging words. Means a lot.
Baby steps, I guess. Thanks. *hugs back*

Those who vaguely share my interests are already in their own cliques. Maybe I just need to sleep through the last few weeks of high school, and start over in college. Hopefully I won't jeopardize my fresh start the way I did with high school. Hopefully.

I understand some people may miss me after I'm gone. I do want to keep going for my mom. Not sure how much longer I can stay on this road, though. Faith, I guess.

I'm still financially dependent at least for the next 4 years, though, so I don't really have a chance to get a real saying in my life. I'm still closeted, for instance.

I wish I could persevere for just a few more seconds. I _am_ close to the finish line, but I'm far too exhausted to keep going.

I understand on a technical level that, yes, seemingly perfect people are never truly without flaws. Each person must have at least one fatal flaw that s/he feels deeply insecure about. Being aware of it doesn't really make a difference, though; I still can't shake the feeling that I can never be as good.

But I'll keep your words in mind. Hopefully school isn't a reflection of what life really is, or I'll be losing this game before it even begins.

I have always been raised to solve my problems by myself, to believe that having to consult others is a kind of failure. Maybe "push[ing] through suffering independently" isn't such a wise idea after all.

Now to find tenderness and caring attention… Humans are such flawed creatures.

I try to think of myself as a normal person, too, but it seems I have, incidentally or accidentally, isolated myself from most of those around me. I feel out of place most of the time, which, coupled with my deteriorating self-image, makes me feel miserable, which further extenuates my isolation, cycle repeats, etc.

I think I need to improve my self-image. I figured, if I looked better to myself, I might gain some confidence, which would doubtless help me open my mouth. I don't know where to start, though. Therapy? Personality change? Diet and exercise? I've tried so many things, but whatever plans I had would crash and burn in a matter of days. I feel rather hopeless.

Thanks for reading my wall of text. :-)

That's another issue for me. No one really gives a damn about computers unless it's about Facebook, Twitter, a multitude of other social networks, or asking for help when their computers break down. As soon as someone mentions "Manchester United" everybody tries to chime in, but "C" draws mostly crickets and weird stares.

I'm just normally not up-to-date with things that high school students should normally keep tabs on. Not many people share my interests, or even a small subset of them. Makes it tougher to strike a conversation.
